concepts.name: Force as a vector
concepts.summary: Recognise force as a quantity with magnitude, direction and point of application, and state its units and line of action.

concepts.name: Newton's first and third laws
concepts.summary: Explain that a body at rest has zero net force and that contact forces occur in equal and opposite pairs.

concepts.name: Resolving forces into components
concepts.summary: Break a force into perpendicular x and y components and rebuild it from them using trigonometry.

concepts.name: Resultant of concurrent forces
concepts.summary: Explain how several forces acting at one point combine into a single equivalent force.

concepts.name: Moment of a force
concepts.summary: Describe the moment as force times perpendicular distance about a point and give its sense as clockwise or counterclockwise.

concepts.name: Rigid body and particle idealisation
concepts.summary: Recall that statics treats bodies as non-deforming and when a body can be modelled as a particle.

concepts.name: Common support types
concepts.summary: Name pin, roller and fixed supports and recall which reaction forces or moments each can provide.

misconceptions.text: A body at rest has no forces acting on it.
A moment depends only on the size of the force, not on where it acts.
The magnitude of a resultant is always the arithmetic sum of the force magnitudes.

concepts.name: Free-body diagram construction
concepts.summary: Isolate a body and draw all applied and reaction forces on it with chosen axes and dimensions.

concepts.name: Particle equilibrium equations
concepts.summary: Apply force sums in each direction to find unknown forces or angles for a particle in equilibrium.

concepts.name: Moment by vector cross product
concepts.summary: Compute the moment of a force about a point using perpendicular distance, components via Varignon, or the cross product.

concepts.name: Couples and couple moments
concepts.summary: Calculate the moment of a couple and apply that it is the same about every point.

concepts.name: Distributed load replacement
concepts.summary: Replace a distributed load with an equivalent resultant acting at the centroid of the load diagram.

concepts.name: Equilibrium of rigid bodies in 2D
concepts.summary: Use the three planar equilibrium equations to solve for support reactions of a single rigid body.

concepts.name: Two-force members
concepts.summary: Recognise that a member loaded at two points only carries force along the line joining them.

misconceptions.text: A free-body diagram should include the forces the body exerts on its surroundings.
The moment of a couple depends on the point about which it is taken.
A distributed load acts at the midpoint of the beam regardless of its shape.

concepts.name: Equivalent force-couple systems
concepts.summary: Reduce any force and couple system to a single resultant force and couple at a chosen point, or to a single force.

concepts.name: Three-dimensional equilibrium
concepts.summary: Use vector force and moment sums to solve for reactions of bodies in space, with correct 3D support reactions.

concepts.name: Static determinacy and constraints
concepts.summary: Compare unknowns to equations to classify a body as determinate, indeterminate or improperly constrained.

concepts.name: Truss idealisation and zero-force members
concepts.summary: Analyse truss assumptions (pinned joints, loads at joints) and identify zero-force members by joint inspection.

concepts.name: Method of joints
concepts.summary: Solve for tension or compression in each truss member by applying particle equilibrium joint by joint.

concepts.name: Method of sections
concepts.summary: Cut a truss through chosen members and use moment and force equilibrium of one part to find specific member forces.

concepts.name: Centroids by integration and composite areas
concepts.summary: Locate centroids and centers of gravity of lines, areas and composite bodies using first moments.

misconceptions.text: Every member of a truss must carry load, so zero-force members can be removed.
A member force assumed in the wrong direction means the analysis has failed.
The method of sections can cut through at most three members regardless of the geometry.

concepts.name: Frames and machines analysis
concepts.summary: Separate a frame into members, apply Newton's third law at pins, and solve for internal pin forces and reactions.

concepts.name: Coulomb dry friction
concepts.summary: Distinguish friction as an unknown force up to μsN from impending slip with F=μsN, and analyse sliding versus tipping.

concepts.name: Wedges, screws and belt friction
concepts.summary: Analyse wedges, screws and belts using friction angles and the relation T2=T1 e^(μβ).

concepts.name: Area moments of inertia
concepts.summary: Compute second moments of areas by integration and composite shapes using the parallel-axis theorem.

concepts.name: Product of inertia and principal axes
concepts.summary: Transform inertia values to rotated axes and find principal axes and principal moments.

concepts.name: Fluid pressure and distributed resultants
concepts.summary: Evaluate resultant forces from varying pressure on flat surfaces and use Pappus-Guldinus theorems to judge solution routes.

concepts.name: Solution strategy and checking
concepts.summary: Evaluate alternative equation choices, moment points and limiting cases to judge and verify a statics solution.

misconceptions.text: Friction force always equals μN, even when the body is not about to slip.
In a frame, pin forces on adjoining members need not be equal and opposite.
Moment of inertia of an area depends only on its area, not on its distribution about the axis.

concepts.name: Modelling real structures as idealisations
concepts.summary: Judge when rigid-body, pin-joint, point-load and frictional assumptions are valid and estimate the error when they are not.

concepts.name: Indeterminate structures by compatibility
concepts.summary: Evaluate how adding deformation compatibility to equilibrium resolves redundancies and where statics alone fails.

concepts.name: Virtual work and stability
concepts.summary: Judge equilibrium and its stability of mechanisms using virtual work and potential energy as alternatives to free-body analysis.

concepts.name: Cables and funicular shapes
concepts.summary: Evaluate the shape and tension of cables under distributed and concentrated loads and the link to arches.

concepts.name: Design of a load-resisting system
concepts.summary: Design a truss, frame or support arrangement that carries specified loads with justified member layout and constraints.

concepts.name: Optimising for efficiency and safety
concepts.summary: Create design variants and evaluate them for member forces, friction margins, tipping stability and sensitivity to load uncertainty.

concepts.name: Computational statics formulations
concepts.summary: Formulate equilibrium of a general truss or frame as a linear system and judge its solvability from rank and conditioning.

misconceptions.text: Equilibrium equations are enough to solve any structure that is in equilibrium.
A structure that satisfies equilibrium is automatically stable.
A cable under its own weight forms a parabola exactly.
